about: The guest guard's refused requests: the one table the guard's filter is generated from (go run ./sandbox/internal/guestguard/gen). Numbers are the system call numbers on x86-64 and on aarch64. Every request not listed and not above the ceiling is allowed; the fixed rules (other entries, the x32 bit, request -1, the ceiling) are in package guestguard's assembler.

sources.linux: Linux v7.3, arch/x86/entry/syscalls/syscall_64.tbl (x86-64) and scripts/syscall.tbl (aarch64 and the other generic-table machines), read 2026-11-19; v7.4-rc3 (master 65e4fd942f72) ends at the same 472
sources.gvisor: gVisor release-20260907.0, pkg/sentry/syscalls/linux/linux64.go (its AMD64 and ARM64 tables), read 2026-11-19
sources.design: private/guest-guard-design-2026-11-19.md, Exactly what is refused; its review, private/reviews/guest-guard-design-review-2026-11-19.md, findings 1, 6 and 7

ceiling_why: the highest request number in Linux v7.3's tables (fchroot); a request above it was not reviewed and gets Function not implemented, what an older kernel answers, until the table is reviewed and the ceiling raised (TestCeilingCoversGoSyscallTables trips when Go's tables pass it)
tracing_refused_why: decision 137 of the guard's design, still open; set as its review recommends. everywhere: the rows marked tracing are in every filter. nowhere: they are in none. gvisor: two filters per machine, the plain one without them and the _gvisor one with them, for the wiring to pick by runtime

self_check.why: the guard's own check that its filter is in force (finding guest-guard-13): unshare with every low flag bit set is answered EHWPOISON (133, Memory page has hardware error), which no kernel and no gVisor release answers for unshare (they answer EINVAL for the unknown flags, or EPERM without the right), and which no other filter of a container answers for it: plimsoll's shipped profile and docker's default answer EPERM, unconfined lets the kernel answer EINVAL. When filters are stacked the newest one's errno wins among errno answers, so the guard's 133 shows through any profile that answers this request with an errno. The answer is still a refusal, so a guest that makes the same request gains nothing. Under a profile that kills or traps unshare the guard cannot start anything, and fails closed

requests.name: unshare
requests.why: makes a new namespace, the first step of a private view of the system; refused whole, as the shipped profile does
requests.gvisor: partly supported (time and cgroup namespaces not)

requests.name: clone
requests.why: makes a namespace while starting a child when its flags carry CLONE_NEWNS, NEWCGROUP, NEWUTS, NEWIPC, NEWUSER, NEWPID or NEWNET (the shipped profile's mask); the kernel reads only the flags' low 32 bits, as the filter does

requests.name: clone3
requests.why: its flags are in memory, which a filter cannot read; Function not implemented makes glibc, musl and language runtimes fall back to clone, which is checked

requests.name: setns
requests.why: enters an existing namespace, for instance one another process made

requests.name: mount
requests.why: changes what the filesystem looks like; possible only inside a namespace of the code's own, refused in case another road to one appears

requests.name: umount2
requests.why: the same, taking a mount away

requests.name: pivot_root
requests.why: swaps the root of the filesystem for a folder of the code's own

requests.name: chroot
requests.why: makes a folder the root a process sees

requests.name: open_tree
requests.why: the newer mount interface (Linux 5.2): copies a mount to attach elsewhere

requests.name: move_mount
requests.why: the newer mount interface: attaches a mount

requests.name: fsopen
requests.why: the newer mount interface: starts making a filesystem

requests.name: fsconfig
requests.why: the newer mount interface: configures it

requests.name: fsmount
requests.why: the newer mount interface: turns it into a mount

requests.name: fspick
requests.why: the newer mount interface: reopens a mounted filesystem to change it

requests.name: mount_setattr
requests.why: the newer mount interface: changes a mount's settings

requests.name: open_tree_attr
requests.why: open_tree with settings, new in Linux 6.15

requests.name: fchroot
requests.why: a new form of chroot, new in Linux 7.3; listed so a newer kernel under runc, WSL containers or a Kubernetes runtime does not open it

requests.name: ptrace
requests.why: under gVisor up to at least release-20261116.0 a tracer can rewrite a filtered request after the filter ran (gVisor issue 16093); the shipped runc profile refuses it already

requests.name: process_vm_writev
requests.why: writes another process's memory, the other half of rewriting a request a tracer stopped
